commit_message:
Bug 1931407 - wasm: Rework bytecode handling for compilation to avoid copies. r=yury

We have two problems in bytecode handling:
  1. When streaming compiling, we have dis-contiguous buffers for 'env' 'code' and 'tail'
     regions of bytecode that we parse. This is because while we're background compiling
     the code section we cannot resize that buffer, and so we have a separate 'tail'
     buffer for those bytes as they come off of the wire. However ModuleGenerator::
     finishModule requires the bytecode to be contiguous so we make a big copy of the
     whole module.
      - Then this copy is thrown away if we're not tiering.
      - For eager tiering, we actually create a new copy of just the code section and
        break the bytecode back apart to what we originally had.
  2. When we're doing a synchronous compile, we make a copy of the module bytecode from
     the original array buffer. However there's no need to do this and we could actually
     just decode directly from the array buffer memory.

This commit fixes (1) by switching all of our bytecode handling to work on the (env, code,
tail) version of bytecode and not assume it is contiguous. This is abstracted away in a
new BytecodeSource class which handles the details.

We can fix (2) by making BytecodeSource just have a weak reference to the bytecode, and
adding a BytecodeBuffer class which actually owns the buffers. When we sync compile, we
just use BytecodeSource and never construct a BytecodeBuffer.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D235239

diff --git a/js/src/wasm/WasmBinary.h b/js/src/wasm/WasmBinary.h
index 12a2950d0dbb..631f0d5700d3 100644
--- a/js/src/wasm/WasmBinary.h
+++ b/js/src/wasm/WasmBinary.h
@@ -406,16 +406,16 @@ class Decoder {
         offsetInModule_(offsetInModule),
         error_(error),
         warnings_(warnings) {
     MOZ_ASSERT(begin <= end);
   }
-  explicit Decoder(const Bytes& bytes, size_t offsetInModule = 0,
+  explicit Decoder(BytecodeSpan span, size_t offsetInModule = 0,
                    UniqueChars* error = nullptr,
                    UniqueCharsVector* warnings = nullptr)
-      : beg_(bytes.begin()),
-        end_(bytes.end()),
-        cur_(bytes.begin()),
+      : beg_(span.data()),
+        end_(span.data() + span.size()),
+        cur_(span.data()),
         offsetInModule_(offsetInModule),
         error_(error),
         warnings_(warnings) {}
 
   // These convenience functions use currentOffset() as the errorOffset.

findings.title: Use-after-free: wasm bytecode pointer captured before FeatureOptions::init can detach the backing buffer
findings.message: WebAssembly_validate (and the sibling WasmModuleObject::construct / WebAssembly_compile paths) call GetBufferSource() first, which unwraps the user-supplied BufferSource object and stores a *raw, non-owning* pointer/length pair (BytecodeSource) directly into the ArrayBuffer's backing data via SharedMem<uint8_t*> dataPointer. Previously (before this commit) GetBufferSource eagerly copied the bytes into an owned ShareableBytes, so any later detach was harmless. After this refactor ('Rework bytecode handling ... to avoid copies'), BytecodeSource is just a weak reference with no copy at this point. Immediately afterward, the code calls FeatureOptions::init(cx, callArgs.get(1)), which can invoke arbitrary JS (e.g. a Proxy 'get' trap on the second argument object while reading the 'builtins' property). That user-controlled callback can call ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer() on the same buffer referenced by `source`, detaching it and freeing/invalidating the data pointer. The subsequent call to Validate(cx, source, options, &error) (and, in other call sites, CompileBuffer) then dereferences the dangling pointer, leading to a use-after-free read that crashes in js::wasm::DecodeModuleEnvironment when parsing the freed bytes.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) obtain/parse FeatureOptions before grabbing the raw bytecode pointer so any detach happens prior to taking the reference, and/or (b) pin the ArrayBuffer/view's length (JS::PinArrayBufferOrViewLength) for the duration of compilation/validation so it cannot be detached while BytecodeSource/BytecodeBuffer holds a weak reference to it, releasing the pin once compilation completes.

ground_truth.root_cause: A refactor (bug 1931407) changed bytecode handling from an eager, owning copy of the ArrayBuffer contents into a non-owning weak reference (BytecodeSource) to avoid redundant copies for performance. This removed the implicit safety property that the previous code had (the data was already copied before any further JS could run). The new code paths then call into user-controllable JS (FeatureOptions::init, which parses an options object that can be a Proxy) after capturing the raw pointer but before using it, creating a window where the buffer can be detached/freed out from under the still-held pointer.
